description:
Apply the proposed mapping to the order — the print suppliers' record.

Call only after the customer's approval has been recorded: answer the
`APPROVE_MAPPING` confirmation with `prepress_confirm` first, unless the
mapping card already did (the item is `approved`). This is the step that
commits. Requires a `PROPOSED` mapping, approved.

Returns a `job_id`. This waits for page management to finish, so the
result usually reports `configured: true` and no follow-up is needed. If
it reports `configured: false` the mapping is applied and still
processing — call `prepress_check_configuration` later, and never
re-submit.

Job errors: `OrderNotMappableError` (the order has moved past awaiting
artwork — mapping is no longer possible), `MappingNotApprovedError` (the
customer hasn't approved yet — answer the `APPROVE_MAPPING` confirmation
with `prepress_confirm`), `MappingNotProposedError`, `MappingRejectedError`
(a file changed since
the proposal — re-run `prepress_map_pages`), or
`UnrepresentableMappingError`, or `ItemHasDesignError` (the item holds an
attached design, and the design is what prints).

A submitted mapping is what prints for the item, so the design and
candidates made for it are released: the next item can be designed.
name: prepress_submit_mapping

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Submit the page mapping
